title: The mysterious exception
summary: Read a runtime stack trace, find the failing access, and repair the function.

scenario.briefing: customerLabel crashes for guest orders. The stack trace points at a property access. Repair the function so missing customer data produces Guest while real names are preserved.

objectives.description: Handle missing customer data without hiding real names.
Check understanding through the remaining explanation and transfer evidence.

hints: The trace says it cannot read a property of undefined.
order.customer may be missing for guest orders.
Guard customer before reading name, and fall back to Guest.
Use optional chaining and nullish fallback: const name = order.customer?.name ?? "Guest"; return name.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a network fault because the data is remote.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Blames the remote data source instead of the local order.customer access that threw.
misconceptions.feedback: The stack trace points to a local property access. The network delivered data without a customer, but the crash happens in this function.

misconceptions.description: Swallowing every error to stop the crash.
misconceptions.feedback: Blanket suppression hides real faults and can replace a real name with Guest. Handle the specific missing-value case and keep other failures visible.

misconceptions.description: Believing a broad catch block is always the safest repair.
misconceptions.feedback: A broad catch treats unrelated faults as the known missing-value case. Prefer specific handling and let unexpected errors surface.

sections.title: Stack traces point to evidence
sections.body: A runtime error includes a message and a stack trace. The message names the operation that failed; the trace lists the call path. Start at the topmost line in your own code and inspect the values that reach it.

sections.title: Handle the expected case precisely
sections.body: Guest orders legitimately lack a customer record. That case can default to Guest. A broad try/catch around everything would also hide programming errors, making future defects harder to find.

vocabulary.definition: A runtime condition that interrupts normal execution.
A report of the call path that led to an error.
A syntax that stops a property access when the base is missing.

hints: Use the stack trace to choose the instruction that actually threw, then the smallest repair.
A property access on undefined throws; the fix should handle that specific missing value.
If user.profile is missing, user.profile.name throws, while user.profile?.name ?? "Guest" is safe.
The failing instruction reads order.customer.name; choose the optional-chain fix rather than a catch-all.
steps.title: Find the failing line
steps.prompt: Given the stack trace and function, choose the faulty instruction and the smallest repair.

fixes.label: Wrap the function body in try { } catch { return "Guest"; }
Remove the function and return "Guest" every time

steps.explanation: The crash happens when order.customer is missing. Optional chaining plus a nullish fallback handles that case without hiding unrelated faults.

hints: Return the customer's name when present and Guest for every missing case.
Optional chaining plus nullish coalescing handles a missing customer or name.
For {customer: null}, customer?.name is undefined, and ?? "Guest" supplies the fallback.
Use optional chaining on customer and a nullish fallback, so a real name survives and a missing customer or name becomes Guest.
steps.title: Repair customerLabel
steps.prompt: Edit labels.js. Return the customer name when it exists, otherwise Guest. Run the tests.

tests.description: A customer without a name becomes Guest.
tests.name: customerLabel

hints: Select statements about tracing and handling exceptions.
A stack trace narrows the path; specific handling preserves evidence of unrelated faults.
Catching every error in a function can hide a typo that should fail loudly.
Three statements are accurate; reject the claim that a broad catch is always safest.
steps.title: Handle the case, not everything

statements.label: A stack trace narrows the call path but does not by itself prove the root cause.
Handling a known missing value is better than suppressing every exception.
A broad catch block is always the safest repair.
Reproducing the failing input makes the bug easier to verify.

steps.explanation: Specific handling preserves evidence of unexpected faults. Reproduction gives a reliable way to confirm the repair.

accessibility.summary: The stack trace and instructions are plain text. Fault and repair choices use radio groups.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Choose the line and repair with arrow keys. Ctrl+Enter runs code tests.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: The stack trace is read as a code block. Each test announces its input case and expected label.
